title: AWS re:Invent 2025 - Spec-driven development with Kiro  (DEV314)
summary: AWS re:Invent code talk building a job-interview app in Kiro with spec-driven development, hooks and property-based tests.

assertions.quote: planning upfront really helped the models focus and produce better output

verdicts.note: Plan-then-execute consistently reduces agent rework in practice and in vendor evals, especially on multi-file tasks.

assertions.quote: adding these property-based testing makes the output of your code at a much higher quality and oftentimes less bugs

verdicts.note: Property-based testing is a strong verification technique and pairs well with explicit invariants; vendor-reported gains, and property quality still depends on how well they're written.

assertions.quote: you have to read it and pay attention to what it's doing. Because otherwise it will do things that we don't expect

verdicts.note: Given documented defect and security rates in AI code, human review before merge is standard practice (e.g. Amazon's two-person rule for AI-assisted changes); it's a sound norm.
The paper recommends careful review of AI code whatever the tool, along with static analysis, tests, security checks, and monitoring after merge.

Human-in-the-loop review is recommended by 48% of 33 safeguard sources, but the review says few studies show whether such safeguards actually reduce risk, so they are 'recommended rather than proven'.
In Google's practice humans review LLM-generated code like any other code, and in the int64 migration humans had to revert some incorrect or unnecessary model changes in most cases.

Projects that merge more pull requests without any code review show a larger post-merge corrective-maintenance burden from agentic code (about 6% per 10 percentage points of no-review rate across 177 projects); this supports keeping a review gate, but the design is correlational and cannot separate review from other project practices, nor human from automated review.

assertions.quote: you first start with a skateboard and move to a bike and then build a car ... you always have something that's workable

verdicts.note: Tracer-bullet/vertical slicing gives earlier integration feedback; applies to agents as to humans.

assertions.quote: the agent is able to read it ... ever since we've added this diagnostics tool, it's been really great

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.
